title: Idle load-to-use latency ladder by access path (extractor B, blind)
conventions: All values are idle (unloaded) latency in ns, read from printed numbers (no chart reads). Rows are sorted by latency, fastest first. kind=measured (filled), estimate (spec arithmetic or projection, hollow), modelled (Berger component model, hollow). Platforms differ across rows; compare within a row. '>' lower bounds are kept as lo/hi with bound noted. Estimate rows are separate entries (overlay_on names the measured row they sit on). RDMA rows differ in granularity: Octopus 64 B cacheline via ToR, Fastswap 4 KB page read, PolarCXLMem 64 B read.

xeon_max.text: arXiv 2505.14294 prints only a relative result: on-package HBM has 'about 20 % higher memory latency compared to DDR' (single-core pointer chase, Fig. 3, y-axis latency in ns plotted vs window size, no printed values) and achieved bandwidth 'about 700 GB/s and 200 GB/s respectively' (HBM2e vs DDR5; STREAM, Fig. 2). Row left out; keep the slide callout relative.
xeon_max.loc: PDF p.1 abstract-level text and Fig. 2/3 captions

switch_adder.text: Octopus: a CXL switch 'adds at least 220 ns'. PolarCXLMem: 549 - 265.2 = 283.8 ns (local socket); 651 - 345.9 = 305.1 ns (remote socket).
switch_adder.unc: derived: switch-latency minus no-switch latency on the same socket, PolarCXLMem Table 1

first_hop_adder.text: Measured adders over local DRAM: Octopus 230-270 vs 115 (+115-155); Vistara 250 vs 130 (+120); Melody 214-394 vs local 111-117 on the same SPR/EMR hosts (+97 to +283); PolarCXLMem 265.2 vs 146 (+119.2) local socket, 345.9 vs 231 (+114.9) remote socket.
first_hop_adder.unc: derived: CXL idle minus local-DRAM idle on the same platform

extraction.agent_b: extractor B, blind; did not open latency_ladder.json
extraction.method: pdftotext -layout on the full-text PDFs; every number is a printed value in text or a table; no chart reads. Octopus, Melody, Vistara, Das Sharma, Xeon Max PDFs and the Chips and Cheese HTML were fetched into fulltext/. ByteDance rows added as supplementary notes.

caveats: Platforms differ across rows; only compare within a row.
NVMe upper bound 50 us rests on an unread Micron spec snippet; TPP Fig. 2 prints 10-40 us.
Chips and Cheese rows are [S]; GH200 value is printed as 'under 300', plotted at 300. The H100 330 ns is the PCIe H100 measured in an earlier Chips and Cheese run, restated in the GH200 article.
Xeon Max absolute ns not printed; row omitted.
Berger 270/345 are lower bounds ('>'); Pond/Berger 155/180 are model outputs, not measurements.

Octopus Fig. 2 'CXL expansion' (230-270) is on Xeon 6 and AMD Turin; Octopus Fig. 4 table gives Xeon 5/6 P50 for four named devices (CXL-A 215/255, CXL-D 230/270, CXL-B 275/315, CXL-C 390/435), not used.
Do not plot MemChannel 220.5 ns switched figure (FLAG G4); not extracted.
Cable adder (Levis HotNets'23) and Pond/TPP numbers beyond those listed were not part of this extraction.
